clue.text: Support in reverse

definitions.meaning: support given to a cause or person, as in financial help
travelling backwards, as a driver does in reverse gear

explanation.surface: Someone offering backing while going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing is support or endorsement, and backing a car is moving it in reverse.

clue.text: Born and brought up to be prepared for dinner

parts.note: a child is raised when brought up

explanation.surface: A life story of birth and upbringing that ends in being cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Braising is slow cooking in a covered pot, a way of preparing a meal.

clue.text: Boil stone

definitions.meaning: a painful pus-filled swelling on the skin
a precious gem, typically a cut red garnet

explanation.surface: A medical note about a boil and a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is both a large skin abscess and a red gemstone such as a garnet.

clue.text: The assembly follows one up in a poem

indicators.note: follows puts the assembly piece after the one piece

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: A parliament succeeds someone, raised up in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the Irish parliament's name, and 'follows' puts it after the numeral. The Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic about the siege of Troy is a famous poem.

clue.text: Have a look, having backed a coloured horse

indicators.note: having backed tells us the coloured horse is read in reverse

parts.note: red is a colour
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A punter looks over the form after betting on a chestnut horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing sense of 'backed', putting money on a horse, is the misdirection: here it reverses the whole coloured horse. Taking a gander is informal British for having a look.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a gander is an informal idiom for having a quick look.

clue.text: Birds a doctor gives jabs to

parts.note: MO is medical officer, a common crossword doctor
to jab at someone is to poke them

explanation.surface: A medic going round injecting birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The morepork is a small owl of New Zealand and Australia, spelt this way as well.

clue.text: Something extinct going from graduates to university teacher

parts.note: MAs are Masters of Arts, holders of a degree
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Academic progress from degree holders to lecturers.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastodon was a prehistoric elephant-like animal that died out.

clue.text: A quantity of paper supplied like water is a figment of the imagination

parts.note: water is piped to homes
a ream is a set quantity of paper sheets, usually five hundred

explanation.surface: Stationery delivered through the mains turns out to be imaginary.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is a fanciful, unrealistic hope.

clue.text: Measure about the present acquainted with

indicators.note: about means the measure goes around the present

parts.note: kn is the abbreviation for knot, a measure of speed at sea
now is the present moment

explanation.surface: Gauging the current time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something known is familiar, a thing one has met with.

clue.text: Southern writers concerned with rising poet

parts.note: pens are writing instruments

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Authors from the south dealing with an up-and-coming versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns RE into ER. Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was an Elizabethan writer of verse.

clue.text: To call to account is a sound rule

indicators.note: sound tells us the words before and after are to be heard as speech, not read as letters

parts.note: a monarch's reign is a period of rule

explanation.surface: A claim that bringing someone to book is a just principle.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, 'a reign' sounds the same as the answer; the split shown puts the A in front and lets the second syllable carry the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to bring a person before a court to answer a charge.

clue.text: Imagine the attitude after a mouthful

indicators.note: after places the attitude piece behind the mouthful piece in the answer

parts.note: a sup is a small mouthful of drink
a pose is a bodily attitude or posture

explanation.surface: Picture the stance someone strikes after taking a sip.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose something is to assume or picture it in the mind.

clue.text: Broadcasting activities for making reliable archives?

definitions.meaning: work done in radio studios capturing audio
sound can mean reliable and records are archived documents

explanation.surface: Radio work described as a way of keeping trustworthy files.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: sound means reliable, and recordings are records kept as archives.
explanation.definitionFit: Studio work captures audio for transmission, and read as sound plus records it describes dependable archives.

clue.text: Leave secretly for some time with a politician

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December, a stretch of time
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician slips away for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart suddenly and furtively, often to avoid trouble.

clue.text: Without moving house an animal provides home for others

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the animal goes around the other piece

parts.note: a mole is a burrowing animal

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters of house are shifted around

explanation.surface: A creature stays put but shelters others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old word for outside, so the animal wraps round the rearranged house signalled by 'moving'. The 'others' are mice.
explanation.definitionFit: The others are mice, for whom a small hole in a skirting board is the home.

clue.text: When no irregular verb holds me back

indicators.note: holds means the jumbled letters wrap around the other piece
irregular tells us the letters of no and verb are in a jumbled, not orderly, sequence
back tells us the word me is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A grammar puzzle about an irregular verb containing a pronoun backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' turns NO and VERB into NOVBER, which 'holds' EM, the reversal of ME signalled by 'back'. The definition 'When' asks for a time.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh month is a time, answering the question of when something happens.

clue.text: Performance of actors who don't travel on motorways?

parts.note: drivers on a B-road are off the motorway network, a minor British road
the cast is the company of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A touring company that avoids the big roads.
explanation.walkthrough: B-roads are British secondary roads, below motorways and A-roads, read here as B ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast is a programme transmitted on radio or television, a performance on air.

clue.text: For the hard-working it includes information on the back cover

indicators.note: on the back tells us the cover word is read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover

indicators.note: includes means it wraps around the information

parts.note: taken as written
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Advice for the industrious: the blurb on the back cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the back' turns LID into DIL. GEN is British informal for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligent describes someone careful and industrious in their work.

clue.text: Angelic, turning a rich cube

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of the following words are rotated into a new order

explanation.surface: Something heavenly about spinning a valuable cube.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubs are child-like angels, so a cherubic face looks innocent and angelic.

clue.text: Arrived with destiny in royal seat

parts.note: came means arrived
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: Coming to the throne by fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot was King Arthur's legendary court and castle.

clue.text: The meaning of something foreign

definitions.meaning: the ... of a remark is its significance
a product brought in from another country

explanation.surface: The significance of a thing from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Import is the sense or significance of something, and also goods brought in from abroad.

clue.text: Made appointment with testy doctor

annotationWithheld.why: Made appointment with testy doctor: TRYSTED is TESTY plus DR rearranged, so 'doctor' must give DR and signal the anagram at once, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Fungus which almost makes a Middle Eastern potentate wealthy

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish or Ottoman commander or chief

indicators.note: almost tells us the last letter of the wealthy word is lost

parts.note: rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A mushroom that nearly makes an Ottoman chief rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Agarics are gill-bearing mushrooms such as the fly agaric.

clue.text: In a month in the grounds which are reorganised for a day

annotationWithheld.why: In a month in the grounds which are reorganised for a day: the likely fodder IN A + M(onth) + THE GROUNDS lacks the Y of the answer, and no reading of the held words supplies it, so the clue appears garbled in the OCR
annotationWithheld.clue: In a month in the grounds which are reorganised for a day

clue.text: Animal which starts getting more important in rank

indicators.note: in places that opening letter inside the rank word

parts.note: a tier is a rank or level in a hierarchy

indicators.note: starts picks out the opening letter of getting

explanation.surface: A creature that begins climbing the hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more important' is surface padding about rising in rank; the first letter of 'getting' goes inside TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is a large striped wild cat.

clue.text: Improper component of shotgun duels

indicators.note: component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something unseemly about duelling with shotguns.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means unwarranted or inappropriate, excessive beyond what is proper.

clue.text: Organ which shows a famous communist left in a toboggan

indicators.note: in places the communist and left pieces inside the toboggan

parts.note: a luge is a small racing toboggan
Ho Chi Minh, the Vietnamese communist leader, is often clued as HO

explanation.surface: A Vietnamese leader with a lefty sledging down a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is slang: the word is informal British for an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the ear, the organ of hearing.

clue.text: New version of socialist transport

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of left-wing socialists
a raft is a simple means of water transport

explanation.surface: A fresh take on public transport policy from the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A redraft is a revised text, written again after changes.

clue.text: Kind of punishment for people in the wrong

indicators.note: in tells us people sit inside the wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men means people in general

explanation.surface: Sentencing those who are at fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe suffering inflicted on someone, a form of punishment.

clue.text: Belief about thanks being returned when it is manufactured

indicators.note: about means the belief word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a creed is a set of beliefs

indicators.note: being returned tells us the thanks word is sent back, read in the other direction

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A creed about gratitude coming back once a thing is made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it is' links the wordplay to the definition. 'being returned' sends the thanks word back, and 'about' wraps the belief round it. TA is British informal for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something manufactured has been made or brought into existence.
